Situation1: Their partner had a mildly stressful day at work and mentions it casually.
Expectation2: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation2: A friend sends a text message complaining about having a long, boring day.
Story: I walked through the door, setting my bag down just as my husband sighed from the couch. He told me about his day—nothing dramatic, just a string of small annoyances at work. I could see he wanted me to listen, maybe offer a hug or a few comforting words. As I sat beside him, my phone buzzed. It was a message from my friend, Sarah: “Ugh, today was endless. I need to vent. Can you talk?” I stared at the screen, feeling the weight of her words. She’d been having a rough week, and I knew she counted on me to be there, to listen and reassure her. But right now, my husband was looking at me, waiting for me to be present for him. My heart tugged in two directions—toward the man I love, who needed my attention, and toward my friend, who was reaching out for support. I felt the pressure building, unsure how to be what both of them needed at the same time.
